[MUQATIL:80:8-17/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The person who comes striving in the heat and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktūm.
[MUQATIL:80:8-17/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God admonishes the Prophet to stop attending to those who feel self-sufficient and to welcome, rather than turn from, the person who comes fearing his Lord.
[MUQATIL:80:8-17/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | After the revelation concerning Ibn Umm Maktūm, the Prophet honored him and appointed him deputy over Medina twice during military expeditions.
[NAHHAS:v5p149/r14] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The verbal clauses at verses 8 and 9 can be circumstantial accusatives; the latter clause may also be another predicate.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r14] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The man who comes eagerly to seek knowledge and fears God is neglected while the Prophet turns elsewhere and occupies himself with others.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p392/r15] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The whole passage is a reproach directed to the Prophet on behalf of the poor.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p213#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | rejects | He rejects the suggestion that the Prophet turned toward the wealthy for their riches: the verse says the other man came striving and fearing, not that he was poor.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p215#2/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس، والكلبي، ومقاتل | reports | They understand the man's striving as seeking God's pleasure and doing good that pleases Him.
[DAMGHANI:v1p237/r2] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Saʿy can mean moving quickly or hurrying. | mentions 36:20, 20:20, 28:20
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن وجماعة | reports | They say it was revealed when Ibn Umm Maktūm interrupted the Prophet's effort to convert Meccan leaders; the Prophet turned back to them and God rebuked him.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن وجماعة | reports | Afterward the Prophet honored him, welcomed him as the man over whom his Lord reproached him, and asked his needs.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أنس | reports | Anas says he saw Ibn Umm Maktūm at al-Qādisiyya in armor with a black banner.
[JISHUMI:v10p7280/r7] JISHUMI, d. 494 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd relates the saying that if the Messenger concealed revelation, he would have concealed this passage.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p336/r9] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The person who comes hastening is Ibn Umm Maktum.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p701/r19] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Yasʿā means that the poor man hastens in seeking good.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r13] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | يسعى can mean walking, or striving in one's affairs, religious practice, and approach to the Prophet.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r21] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The immediate context concerns Quraysh's disbelievers and Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, but the lesson also applies to anyone sharing their qualities.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p437/r22] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | People of religious learning are instructed to bring near the righteous weak and prefer them over socially noble people lacking goodness.
[TABRISI:80:1-23#2/r13] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The man who comes eagerly, strives for good, and fears God is Ibn Umm Maktum.
[TABRISI:80:20/r10] TABRISI, d. 548 · المرتضى علم الهدى | rejects | Al-Murtada rejects identifying the passage's subject as the Prophet: the text does not name him, and frowning at a believing seeker or preferring rich people to the poor conflicts with his noble character.
[TABRISI:80:20/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | The passage is said to have been revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, also named Abdullah ibn Shurayh ibn Malik ibn Rabiʿa al-Fihri, when he came as the Prophet was urging Quraysh leaders toward Islam.
[TABRISI:80:20/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | The Prophet was speaking with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAbbas, Ubayy, and Umayya ibn Khalaf when Ibn Umm Maktum repeatedly asked to be taught; the Prophet turned away, thinking the leaders might scorn a following of blind people and slaves.
[TABRISI:80:20/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Afterward the Prophet honored Ibn Umm Maktum, greeted him as the man for whom his Lord had reproached him, asked about his needs, and appointed him deputy in Medina twice.
[TABRISI:80:20/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · أنس بن مالك | reports | Anas ibn Malik says he saw Ibn Umm Maktum at al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black standard.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | The first of two views takes yasʿa to mean that he walks.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p28#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | The second view says his striving means doing good; this is Ibn Umm Maktum, who fears God.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p52#5/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Yasʿā means that the man hastens in seeking good, as in the command to hasten to Friday prayer, 62:9. | mentions 62:9
[QURTUBI-FULL:80:5-10/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The person who comes eagerly is seeking knowledge for God's sake.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:80:3-8/r11] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | This is the person who comes swiftly seeking good.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p317#6/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The man hurries to the Prophet in pursuit of good.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p407/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The man who comes striving is hurrying in pursuit of his religion.
[SAMIN-DURR:80:8/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | يسعى is a circumstantial clause for the subject of جاءك; وهو يخشى is another circumstance for the subject of يسعى, a circumstance within a circumstance. Treating it as a second coordinated circumstance is weak.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The blind man came purposefully and feared God, seeking guidance from what the Prophet taught, but the Prophet was occupied with another person.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p319#2/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God directs the Prophet to warn everyone equally, without favoring the eminent over the weak, rich over poor, masters over slaves, men over women, or adults over children; God guides whom He wills.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p322#s080/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The surah explains the call to warn those who fear by using resurrection to purify receptive hearts; human creation and the cycle of food prove God’s power, making rejection astonishing. | mentions 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو جعفر بن الزبير | reports | Ibn al-Zubayr connects this opening to the prior calls to heed and fear: humble people whom the world overlooks are especially cared for and chosen by God. | mentions 79:26, 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | The saying that a disheveled, dusty person whom people ignore could swear an oath that God would fulfill illustrates the hidden rank of the humble.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | reports | Ibn Umm Maktūm was the Prophet’s muezzin and the man whose visit occasioned the sūra’s admonition.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The rebuke teaches the Prophet to remain patiently with people like Ibn Maktūm and not to despise them, echoing other admonitions and the command not to drive away those who seek God. | mentions 18:28, 39:65, 38:88, 31:18
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p325/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Ibn Maktūm sought instruction while the Prophet addressed a Quraysh notable whose conversion he hoped would save the man and his kin; attending to that hope led him to neglect the immediate visitor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The Prophet’s slight distraction from the sincere seeker for elite prospects cannot benefit the religion as much as the seeker’s evident readiness.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The dropped tā in the verb indicates that the distraction is slight.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The poor seeker comes quickly, eager for the good and reminder of God that the Prophet offers.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The seeker’s arrival and fear contrast with the rich man’s failure to come and lack of fear, warning against favoring the wealthy and slighting a sincere visitor.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The verbal form depicts someone coming urgently and seeking good; a person who approaches and presses through the crowd to reach the Prophet has a great claim on him.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326#2/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The passage uses ḥtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor second, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first case.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The description of the Prophet as a warner to those who fear applies to Ibn Umm Maktūm. | mentions 79:45
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p326/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The command to keep company with those who call upon God morning and evening is another passage revealed in the pattern of Ibn Umm Maktūm’s case. | mentions 18:28
[DURR-FULL:v8p415/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عائشة | reports | In another account, ʿAʾisha says the Prophet was addressing Quraysh leaders including Abu Jahl and ʿUtba when Ibn Umm Maktum came; the Prophet turned away, and the quoted passage was revealed. | mentions 80:5, 80:6, 80:7, 80:8, 80:9, 80:10
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The seeker comes quickly, eager for the guidance, religious rulings, and good qualities available from the Prophet.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r10] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | reports | A report says the Prophet thereafter never frowned at a poor person or sought out a rich one, and the poor held an honored place in his gathering.

ds | The episode instructs scholars, judges, and rulers to draw a weak seeker of good near and prefer him over a prominent person lacking good.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r12] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | Some say the passage honors poverty and its people while devaluing worldly status; companionship with sincere, detached poor people benefits, unlike companionship with the rich.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r13] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الحديث | reports | A hadith says that favoring a rich person by treating a poor person unjustly destroys a third of one’s religion.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r14] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Taḥāmala can mean enduring something with difficulty, or treating another person unjustly.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r15] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعض الأكابر | reports | Some great Sufis explain that the Prophet honored Quraysh’s chiefs as manifestations of divine majesty, while a higher station is to see no distinction among people under God’s absolute reality.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r16] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The higher instruction is to remain with those who call on God morning and evening, as stated later in the Quran. | mentions 18:28
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r17] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الله تعالى | reports | Bursevi invokes the divine saying about the hungry and thirsty person whom people failed to feed and give drink.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · سعدي المفتي | reports | Saʿdī al-Muftī sees an ellipsis by ihtibāk: mentioning the rich first implies the poor, while the seeker’s coming and fear imply their opposites in the first clause.
[BURSEVI:v10p259/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The account teaches that worth lies in souls and spiritual states, not outward appearance or wealth: faith makes the socially lowly noble, while unbelief makes the socially esteemed wretched.
[ALUSI-FULL:v30p41#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | He comes hastening, seeking from the Prophet guidance's rulings and qualities of good.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The clause about the one who comes is coordinated with the self-sufficient person as the opposing side, completing the division by contrasting opposites. | mentions 80:5
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r11] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The one who comes eagerly is Ibn Umm Maktūm, confirming the account in the opening verses. | mentions 80:1, 80:2
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p108/r12] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Saʿy is brisk walking, used for eagerness to meet; it contrasts with the self-sufficient person’s aversion to receiving the Prophet’s attention. | mentions 80:5
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | This clause contrasts with verse 5 and completes the division by setting opposites against each other; it also reinforces the opening account of the blind man’s visit. | mentions 80:1, 80:2, 80:5
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r11] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The man who comes eagerly is Ibn Umm Maktūm.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p138#7/r12] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Saʿy is brisk walking, used here for eagerness to meet the Prophet; this contrasts with the self-sufficient man’s disdain for being approached. | mentions 80:5
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | The proposed honorific reading of the switch from third to second person does not fit the direct address that follows, whose rebuke is stronger and has no conciliatory intimacy.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The rebuked pattern is that the Prophet attends to wealthy people who scorn the truth, unconcerned whether they purify themselves, while neglecting the person earnestly seeking purification and fearing God.
[TABATABAI:80:5-12/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Saʿy literally means walking quickly; in context the man comes hastening to remember and purify himself through religious learning.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p169/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | ʿAbasa pairs with al-Nāziʿāt and shares its central theme, discourse style, and reasoning; the changed sequence of topics gives this sūrah its distinct majesty. | mentions 79:45
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The word yasʿā means to act zealously, not necessarily to run; in 62:9 it means turning eagerly to God’s word, like a thirsty person approaching a fountain. | mentions 62:9
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p177/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The indifferent are absorbed in worldly pleasures and do not consider the afterlife, whereas those who fear meeting God are receptive; the Prophet pursued the former while neglecting the latter.

<<end of notes>>
